quarterly_data.signal: CEO Mike Sicilia on the multicloud database build-out: Oracle has just announced that it has 22 regions live now with Amazon in multi-cloud database, after starting with Azure, then Google, and now Amazon. He noted Q4's over 400% growth in the multi-cloud database business was largely concentrated in the earlier partnerships and NOT in the Amazon partnership, since those regions are only now being delivered.
quarterly_data.figure: 22 regions live now with Amazon in multi-cloud database

quarterly_data.signal: OCI rack form factor: the same technology that makes the Oracle Database portable into competitors' clouds lets Oracle create fully sovereign infrastructure with 12 racks - not an edge solution but full-featured OCI, all of Fusion, all of Oracle's applications. Sicilia: '12 racks is probably high. We’re getting down to six.' He framed this as a low-capital-intensity deployment into banks', utilities' and healthcare systems' existing, already-energized data centers (possibly a chiller retrofit, no new land or power), versus the giga-scale builds that get the headlines.

Forward view on the delivery cadence (asked what changes over the next year): 'we are approaching the sort of peak of our scaled-out infrastructure delivery' and Oracle is 'probably in a position to deliver an industry-leading amount of compute to the market, of scale compute to the market' over that horizon - so proof points around that delivery will be what the market watches.
